added_lemmas.statement:
Let \(x_1,\ldots,x_m\) be independent centered random vectors in \(\mathbb R^p\), let \(S=m^{-1/2}\sum_{j=1}^m x_j\), and let \(G\) be centered Gaussian with \(\operatorname{Cov}(G)=\operatorname{Cov}(S)\).  Suppose that constants \(b_1,b_2>0\) and \(B_m\ge1\) satisfy, for every \(j\le m\) and \(\ell\le p\),
\[
 E\exp(|x_{j\ell}|/B_m)\le2,
 \qquad
 b_1^2\le m^{-1}\sum_{j=1}^mE[x_{j\ell}^2]\le b_2^2,
 \qquad
 m^{-1}\sum_{j=1}^mE[x_{j\ell}^4]\le B_m^2b_2^2.
\]
Then Chernozhukov--Chetverikov--Kato--Koike (2022), Theorem 2.1 and its equivalent hyperrectangle formulation, imply
\[
 \sup_{A\in\mathcal A^{\mathrm{re}}}
 \left|P\{S\in A\}-P\{G\in A\}\right|
 \le C\left\{\frac{B_m^2\log^5(pm)}{m}\right\}^{1/4},
\]
where \(\mathcal A^{\mathrm{re}}\) is the class of axis-aligned hyperrectangles and \(C\) depends only on \(b_1,b_2\).  No positive lower bound on the minimum eigenvalue of \(\operatorname{Cov}(S)\) is required.

source.locator: Theorem 2.1 and the equivalent hyperrectangle formulation in equation (15), pages 2568--2569

added_lemmas.statement:
Fix \(n\) and \(P_n\in\mathcal M_n^{\mathrm{CY},0}\).  Let \(m=|\mathcal Q_n^{\mathrm{IF}}|\), \(p=2K\), \(\epsilon_q=e_q/\sigma_q\), and
\[
 S_{n,k}=\sum_{q\in\mathcal Q_n^{\mathrm{IF}}}a_{kq}\epsilon_q,
 \qquad
 M_n^Z=\max_{k\in\mathcal K_n}|Z_{n,k}|.
\]
Indexing \(q\) arbitrarily, define the sign-expanded summands
\[
 X_q=\sqrt m\,(a_{0q}\epsilon_q,\ldots,a_{K-1,q}\epsilon_q,
 -a_{0q}\epsilon_q,\ldots,-a_{K-1,q}\epsilon_q)\in\mathbb R^p.
\]
Every coordinate of \(m^{-1/2}\sum_qX_q\) has variance one, its maximum is \(\max_k|S_{n,k}|\), and, for a constant \(C\) depending only on \(C_e\),
\[
 B_n=C\sqrt m\,L_n(K),
 \qquad
 \max_{q,j}\|X_{qj}\|_{\psi_1}\le B_n,
 \qquad
 \frac1m\sum_qE_{P_n}X_{qj}^4\le C mL_n(K)^2.
\]
Consequently, with another constant \(C_1\) depending only on \(C_e\),
\[
 \mathfrak g_n^{(5)}
 =C_1\{L_n(K)^2\log^5(((p\vee3)m))\}^{1/4}
\]
satisfies
\[
 \sup_{z\in\mathbb R}
 \left|P_n\{\max_k|S_{n,k}|\le z\}-P\{M_n^Z\le z\}\right|
 \le\mathfrak g_n^{(5)}.
\]
This conclusion permits singular \(\Sigma_n\).

For deterministic \(u\ge0\), define the generic remainder event
\[
 \mathcal R_n(u)=\{\|\rho_n\|_\infty\le u\}.
\]
For \(h\ge0\), let \(\mathcal B_n(h)=\{r_n^{\mathrm{score}}\le h\}\), set \(\delta_h=2h+h^2\), define \(\mathfrak c_n(0)=0\), and, when \(h>0\), put
\[
 \mathfrak c_n(h)=C_3\delta_h^{1/3}
 \{1\vee\log(p/\delta_h)\}^{2/3}.
\]
There are constants \(C_2,C_3<\infty\), depending only on \(C_e\), such that whenever \(0<\delta_h\le1/2\),
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 &\sup_{z\in\mathbb R}\left|P_n\!\left\{
 \max_{k\in\mathcal K_n}\frac{|\widehat\tau_k-\tau_k^{\mathrm{event}}|}{\widehat s_k}\le z
 \right\}-P\{M_n^Z\le z\}\right|\\
 &\quad\le \mathfrak g_n^{(5)}+P_n\{\mathcal R_n(u)^c\}
 +P_n\{\mathcal B_n(h)^c\}
 +C_2\{u\sqrt{\log(2p)}+\delta_h\log(2p)\}
 +\mathfrak c_n(h).
 \end{aligned}
\]
On \(\mathcal B_n(h)\), conditionally on \(Y\), \(W_n^\xi\) is exactly the maximum absolute coordinate of \(N(0,\widehat\Sigma_n)\), and
\[
 \sup_z|P(W_n^\xi\le z\mid Y)-P(M_n^Z\le z)|
 \le\mathfrak c_n(h).
\]
If \(\mathfrak c_n(h)<\min\{\alpha,1-\alpha\}\), then
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 &\left|P_n\{\tau_k^{\mathrm{event}}\in\mathcal C_{n,k}
 \text{ for every }k\in\mathcal K_n\}-(1-\alpha)\right|\\
 &\quad\le1\wedge\Big[\mathfrak g_n^{(5)}+P_n\{\mathcal R_n(u)^c\}
 +2P_n\{\mathcal B_n(h)^c\}\\
 &\hspace{31mm}+C_2\{u\sqrt{\log(2p)}+\delta_h\log(2p)\}
 +2\mathfrak c_n(h)\Big].
 \end{aligned}
\]
The formulas remain valid at \(h=0\) by direct substitution.  Therefore, along any complete array in the baseline event-transfer class \(\mathfrak M^{\mathrm{CY},0}\), if deterministic sequences \(u_n,h_n\downarrow0\) obey
\[
 P_n\{\mathcal R_n(u_n)^c\}\to0,
 \qquad P_n\{\mathcal B_n(h_n)^c\}\to0,
 \qquad u_n\sqrt{\log(2p)}\to0,
 \qquad h_n\log^2(2p)\to0,
\]
then the multiplier band has simultaneous coverage tending to \(1-\alpha\).  This is conditional on the two displayed probability limits.  Under balanced influence loading \(L_n(K)\asymp m^{-1/2}\), the Gaussian-approximation requirement is exactly the elbow
\[
 \log(Km)=o(m^{1/5}).
\]
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
By \(s_k^2=\sum_qc_{kq}^2\sigma_q^2\), \(a_{kq}=c_{kq}\sigma_q/s_k\), and \(s_k>0\) from \(\texttt{ass:horizon-variance-nondegeneracy}\),
\[
 \sum_qa_{kq}^2=1. \tag{1}
\]
The variables \(\epsilon_q=e_q/\sigma_q\) are well defined because \(\sigma_q>0\) by \(\texttt{ass:variance-bounds}\).  They are centered and mutually independent by \(\texttt{ass:centered-errors}\) and \(\texttt{ass:independent-cells}\), satisfy \(E_{P_n}\epsilon_q^2=1\), and obey \(\|\epsilon_q\|_{\psi_2}\le C_e\) by \(\texttt{ass:heteroskedastic-subgaussian}\).  Thus the \(X_q\)'s are independent and centered.  For a coordinate \(j\) associated with horizon \(k\), equation (1) gives
\[
 \frac1m\sum_qE_{P_n}X_{qj}^2
 =\sum_qa_{kq}^2=1. \tag{2}
\]
A sub-Gaussian variable with \(\psi_2\)-norm at most \(C_e\) has fourth moment bounded by a constant depending only on \(C_e\).  Hence
\[
 \frac1m\sum_qE_{P_n}X_{qj}^4
 =m\sum_qa_{kq}^4E_{P_n}\epsilon_q^4
 \le C mL_n(K)^2\sum_qa_{kq}^2
 =C mL_n(K)^2. \tag{3}
\]
Also \(\|X_{qj}\|_{\psi_1}\le C\|X_{qj}\|_{\psi_2}\le C\sqrt mL_n(K)\).  Since (1) implies \(1\le mL_n(K)^2\), the choice \(B_n=C\sqrt mL_n(K)\) is at least one after increasing \(C\).  Equations (2)--(3) verify all moment and scale hypotheses of \(\texttt{lem:cckk2022-gaussian-approximation}\) with fixed \(b_1,b_2\).  Its hyperrectangle inequality applied to the lower rectangles \((-\infty,z]^p\), and to the sign-expanded vector, yields
\[
 \sup_z\left|P_n\{\max_k|S_{n,k}|\le z\}-P\{M_n^Z\le z\}\right|
 \le C\left\{\frac{B_n^2\log^5(((p\vee3)m))}{m}\right\}^{1/4}
 =\mathfrak g_n^{(5)}. \tag{4}
\]
The Gaussian vector in (4) has covariance \(\Sigma_n\) by \(\texttt{lem:staircase-covariance}\).  The cited theorem assumes coordinatewise variance lower bounds, verified by (2), but no positive minimum eigenvalue; thus a singular staircase correlation is allowed.

By the definition of \(\rho_n\), exactly and without a linearization event,
\[
 s_k^{-1}(\widehat\tau_k-\tau_k^{\mathrm{event}})=S_{n,k}+\rho_{n,k}. \tag{5}
\]
Put \(t_k=\widehat s_k/s_k\).  On \(\mathcal B_n(h)\), \(\texttt{thm:heteroskedastic-covariance}\) gives \(|t_k^2-1|\le\delta_h\).  If \(\delta_h\le1/2\), then \(t_k\ge\sqrt{1-\delta_h}>0\), and elementary algebra gives
\[
 |t_k^{-1}-1|
 \le\frac{\delta_h}{\sqrt{1-\delta_h}(1+\sqrt{1-\delta_h})}
 \le\delta_h,
 \qquad t_k^{-1}\le\sqrt2. \tag{6}
\]
Combining (5)--(6), on \(\mathcal R_n(u)\cap\mathcal B_n(h)\),
\[
 \left|\max_k|t_k^{-1}(S_{n,k}+\rho_{n,k})|-\max_k|S_{n,k}|\right|
 \le\delta_h\max_k|S_{n,k}|+\sqrt2u. \tag{7}
\]

Independence, the sub-Gaussian bound, and (1) imply
\(|S_{n,k}\|_{\psi_2}\le C\) uniformly in \(k\).  A union bound therefore gives, for \(0<\delta_h\le1/2\),
\[
 P_n\{\max_k|S_{n,k}|>C_4\sqrt{\log(2p/\delta_h)}\}\le\delta_h. \tag{8}
\]
On the complementary event, the right side of (7) is at most
\[
 v_n=C_5\{\delta_h\sqrt{\log(2p/\delta_h)}+u\}. \tag{9}
\]
The Gaussian vector has unit coordinate variances.  Therefore \(\texttt{lem:cck-gaussian-anti-concentration}\), applied after sign expansion, gives
\[
 \sup_zP\{|M_n^Z-z|\le v_n\}\le C v_n\sqrt{\log(2p)}. \tag{10}
\]
Sandwich the event in (5) studentized by \(\widehat s_k\) between the linear-score events with thresholds \(z-v_n\) and \(z+v_n\).  Equations (4), (8), and (10), together with the union bound for \(\mathcal R_n(u)^c\) and \(\mathcal B_n(h)^c\), yield the asserted distribution inequality after using, for \(0<\delta_h\le1/2\),
\[
 \delta_h+\delta_h\sqrt{\log(2p/\delta_h)\log(2p)}
 \le C\left[\delta_h\log(2p)
 +\delta_h^{1/3}\{1\vee\log(p/\delta_h)\}^{2/3}\right]. \tag{11}
\]
This elementary inequality follows by splitting \(\log(2p/\delta_h)=\log(2p)+\log(1/\delta_h)\), applying \(2\sqrt{ab}\le a+b\), and using \(x\log(1/x)=o(x^{1/3})\) as \(x\downarrow0\), with the remaining compact interval absorbed into the constant.

Conditionally on \(Y\), independence and Gaussianity of the multipliers give
\[
 \operatorname{Cov}\!\left(
 \sum_q\frac{\widehat c_{kq}\widehat\sigma_u}{\widehat s_k}\xi_q,
 \sum_q\frac{\widehat c_{k'q}\widehat\sigma_u}{\widehat s_{k'}}\xi_q
 \mathrel{\Big|}Y\right)=\widehat\Sigma_{kk'}. \tag{12}
\]
Thus \(W_n^\xi\mid Y\) is exactly the maximum absolute coordinate of \(N(0,\widehat\Sigma_n)\).  On \(\mathcal B_n(h)\), the deterministic covariance theorem gives
\[
 \|\widehat\Sigma_n-\Sigma_n\|_{\max}
 \le\frac{2\delta_h}{1-\delta_h}\le4\delta_h. \tag{13}
\]
Applying \(\texttt{lem:cck-gaussian-comparison-maxima}\) to the sign-expanded Gaussian vectors proves the asserted conditional comparison bound.  It also requires only marginal variance nondegeneracy, so singular covariance is harmless.

Let \(F_Z\) be the distribution function of \(M_n^Z\).  The anti-concentration bound makes \(F_Z\) continuous.  On \(\mathcal B_n(h)\), if \(\mathfrak c_n(h)<\min\{\alpha,1-\alpha\}\), the conditional \((1-\alpha)\)-quantile of \(W_n^\xi\) lies between the \((1-\alpha-\mathfrak c_n(h))\)- and \((1-\alpha+\mathfrak c_n(h))\)-quantiles of \(F_Z\).  Apply the preceding feasible-statistic distribution bound at those two deterministic quantiles and add \(P_n\{\mathcal B_n(h)^c\}\).  This gives the finite coverage inequality, including its second copies of the score-event probability and \(\mathfrak c_n(h)\).  When \(h=0\), equations (6) and (13) have zero discrepancy, proving the stated direct-substitution convention.

Finally, the corrected \(\texttt{ass:cell-leverage}\) implies \(\mathfrak g_n^{(5)}\to0\).  The two stated probability limits remove the two event failures.  The condition \(u_n\sqrt{\log(2p)}\to0\) removes the remainder perturbation, and \(h_n\log^2(2p)\to0\) implies both \(\delta_{h_n}\log(2p)\to0\) and \(\mathfrak c_n(h_n)\to0\), using \(x\log^2(1/x)\to0\).  Hence the coverage error tends to zero.  If \(L_n(K)\asymp m^{-1/2}\), then \(L_n(K)^2\log^5(((p\vee3)m))\to0\) is equivalent, up to fixed multiplicative constants inside the logarithm, to \(\log(Km)=o(m^{1/5})\), which proves the elbow statement.

added_lemmas.statement: The published Choi--Yuan model writes \(M^0=M^\star+M^R\), permits nonzero approximation error, imposes global singular-vector incoherence and conditioning, and assumes i.i.d. centered homoskedastic sub-Gaussian noise.  Its staggered-adoption Theorem 3.2 concerns one scalar group-at-time functional and lists six hypotheses: signal, spectral size, missing-block size, approximation bias, global Gram balance, and target-loading nondegeneracy.

source.locator: Section 2, Assumption [Noise], and Theorem 3.2(i)--(vi) in the published author manuscript

attestation.note: Transcribed as a source-scope record from the published author manuscript hosted by PubMed Central; it is not used as a logical proof premise.

added_lemmas.statement:
The event-transfer class \(\mathfrak M^{\mathrm{CY}}\) imposes \(M^R=0\), \(M^0=M^\star=XZ^\top\), exact rank, blockwise uniform geometry, independent row-heteroskedastic noise, variance replication, growing-path leverage, and the primitive band-remainder envelope.  The published Choi--Yuan model-and-scalar-functional class \(\mathfrak M^{\mathrm{CY,pub}}\) instead permits \(M^0=M^\star+M^R\) with \(M^R\ne0\), uses global incoherence and conditioning, assumes i.i.d. homoskedastic sub-Gaussian noise, and imposes the six hypotheses of its scalar staggered-adoption Theorem 3.2.

The band-valid event-transfer class \(\mathfrak M^{\mathrm{CY}}\) and the published Choi--Yuan model-and-scalar-functional class \(\mathfrak M^{\mathrm{CY,pub}}\) are incomparable:
\[
 \mathfrak M^{\mathrm{CY}}\not\subseteq\mathfrak M^{\mathrm{CY,pub}},
 \qquad
 \mathfrak M^{\mathrm{CY,pub}}\not\subseteq\mathfrak M^{\mathrm{CY}}.
\]
The common class is nonempty and obeys
\[
 \varnothing\ne\mathfrak M^{\mathrm{CY,com}}
 \subseteq\mathfrak M^{\mathrm{CY},0}\cap\mathfrak M^{\mathrm{CY,pub}}.
\]
Consequently, if a coverage-frontier converse is witnessed by one array in \(\mathfrak M^{\mathrm{CY,com}}\), that array is admissible for the corresponding supremum over the full published class.  In the other direction, validity of the event-transfer band does not extend by class inclusion to the full published class: a nonzero approximation component \(M^R\) contributes a bias term not present in the event-transfer remainder \(\rho_n\) and must be controlled separately.
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
The two scope descriptions follow directly from \(\texttt{def:cy-event-class}\) and \(\texttt{def:published-choi-yuan-class}\) and their displayed member properties.  We now give explicit complete-array certificates for both noninclusions.
Because every fixed envelope in the event-transfer definition is positive, choose integers \(d_n\uparrow\infty\) recursively fast enough to make each of the finitely many required ratios at index \(n\) no larger than its prescribed envelope.  This diagonal choice is legitimate once the ratios below are shown to converge to zero.

For the event-transfer-only certificate, take one adopting cohort of size \(d_n\), \(d_n^2\) never-treated donors, \(K=1\), adoption at \(g=d_n^2+1\), and \(T=d_n^2+1\), and set \(\tau_{it}=0\) for every cell.  Put \(x_i=z_t=1\), so \(M^0\) has rank one, condition number one, and all block incoherence and normalized Gram eigenvalues equal one.  Let the errors be mutually independent Gaussian variables, with variance one on adopting rows and variance two on donor rows.  They are centered, row-heteroskedastic, uniformly sub-Gaussian, and bounded away from zero and infinity, but they are not identically distributed.

Here \(n_g=d_n\), \(|J_{g0}|=|S_g|=d_n^2\), and the three influence coefficients are respectively \(d_n^{-1}\) on each treated target cell, \(-d_n^{-2}\) on each donor target cell, and \(-d_n^{-3}\) on each treated pre-period cell.  Hence
\[
 s_0^2=d_n^{-1}+2d_n^{-2}+d_n^{-3},
 \qquad
 L_n(1)\le\sqrt2\,d_n^{-1/2},
 \qquad
 |\mathcal Q_n^{\mathrm{IF}}|\le3d_n^3. \tag{1}
\]
It follows that the leverage ratio is \(O(d_n^{-1}\log^5d_n)\).  The variance-replication ratio is \(O(d_n^{-1}\sqrt{\log d_n})\).  Since the rank-one block signal is of order \(d_n^2\), the signal, spectral-size, and missing-block ratios are respectively \(O(d_n^{-1}\sqrt{\log d_n})\), \(O(d_n^{-2}\log^3d_n)\), and \(O(d_n^{-1})\).  Direct substitution in \(R_{g0}^{\mathrm{CY}}\), followed by division by \(s_0\asymp d_n^{-1/2}\), gives
\[
 \Delta_{\mathrm{CY},n}(1)=O(d_n^{-3/2}\log d_n). \tag{2}
\]
All these quantities vanish, so the recursive choice of \(d_n\) places the array in \(\mathfrak M^{\mathrm{CY}}\).  Its two variance values violate the i.i.d. homoskedastic noise property of \(\mathfrak M^{\mathrm{CY,pub}}\).  This proves the first noninclusion.

For the published-only certificate, use the same dimensions, adoption schedule, and zero treatment-effect array, take i.i.d. \(N(0,1)\) noise, and set
\[
 M_n^\star=\mathbf1_N\mathbf1_T^\top,
 \qquad
 M_n^R=\zeta_n w_n v_n^\top, \tag{3}
\]
where \(w_n\perp\mathbf1_N\) and \(v_n\perp\mathbf1_T\) have entries bounded by one and are nonzero.  Choose \(\zeta_n>0\) smaller than the right side of the published approximation condition and small enough that all six published scalar-functional ratios hold.  Such a positive choice exists at every finite \(n\), and it can be made to tend to zero.  The leading matrix in (3) has globally balanced rank-one singular vectors, condition number one, and satisfies the global Gram and target-loading lower bounds.  With dimensions increasing sufficiently fast, the other three published ratios vanish.  Thus the array lies in \(\mathfrak M^{\mathrm{CY,pub}}\).  Orthogonality in (3) gives \(\operatorname{rank}(M_n^0)=2\) for every \(n\), whereas the event-transfer model fixes \(r=1\) and requires \(\operatorname{rank}(M^0)=r\).  Therefore this array is not in \(\mathfrak M^{\mathrm{CY}}\), proving the second noninclusion.

Setting \(\zeta_n=0\) in (3), retaining i.i.d. homoskedastic Gaussian noise, and choosing the same dimensions recursively to satisfy both families of mapped ratios gives a member of \(\mathfrak M^{\mathrm{CY,com}}\).  Hence the common class is nonempty; its two inclusions follow directly from the intersection in \(\texttt{def:cy-common-subclass}\).

If a loss or coverage shortfall is at least \(c>0\) for one law in the common class, then the supremum over the published class is at least that value because the common law is an admissible published law.  This proves upward transfer of a converse.  Conversely, neither noninclusion licenses transfer of an upper guarantee.  In particular, substituting \(M^0=M^\star+M^R\) into a counterfactual error decomposes it into the event-transfer score and remainder plus the omitted approximation contrast induced by \(M^R\); that contrast is identically zero only under \(M^R=0\).  Therefore an additional approximation-bias bound is necessary before the event-transfer upper-band theorem can cover the full published class.

proposed_statement_changes.proposed:
Using the second-order staircase alignment handle, derive a primitive block-ratio expression \(\Delta_n^{\dagger}(K;\eta_n)\) and constants \(0<c<C<\infty\), common across \(n\), such that
\[
 c\Delta_n^{\dagger}(K;\eta_n)\le\Delta_n^*(K;\eta_n)
 \le C\Delta_n^{\dagger}(K;\eta_n)
\]
for every vanishing tail sequence \(\eta_n\), where \(\Delta_n^*\) is optimized over the explicitly defined slice \(\mathcal M_n^{\mathrm{CY},0}\) of the baseline event-transfer class \(\mathfrak M^{\mathrm{CY},0}\).  Establish the conditional coverage frontier in this finite-slice experiment: if there is a deterministic \(h_n\downarrow0\) such that
\[
 \sup_{P_n\in\mathcal M_n^{\mathrm{CY},0}}
 P_n\{\mathcal B_n(h_n)^c\}\to0,
 \qquad h_n\log^2(4K)\to0,
\]
then \(\Delta_n^{\dagger}(K;\eta_n)\sqrt{\log(2K)}\to0\) must imply \(\sup_{P_n\in\mathcal M_n^{\mathrm{CY},0}}\Gamma_n(P_n)\to0\).  Conversely, for every primitive candidate \(\beta\) with \(\beta\triangleleft\Delta^{\dagger}\) and \(\beta_n(K)\sqrt{\log(2K)}\to0\) along a subsequence on which \(\Delta_n^{\dagger}(K;\eta_n)\sqrt{\log(2K)}\) is bounded away from zero, construct one complete staggered low-rank triangular array
\[
 (P_n)_{n\ge1}\in\mathfrak M^{\mathrm{CY,com}}
 \subseteq\mathfrak M^{\mathrm{CY},0}\cap\mathfrak M^{\mathrm{CY,pub}}
\]
such that \(P_n\in\mathcal M_n^{\mathrm{CY},0}\), \(\delta_n(P_n;\eta_n)\ge c\Delta_n^{\dagger}(K;\eta_n)\), \(\liminf_n\Gamma_n(P_n)>0\), and, for some deterministic \(h_n\downarrow0\),
\[
 P_n\{\mathcal B_n(h_n)^c\}\to0,
 \qquad h_n\log^2(4K)\to0.
\]
The derivation must first test whether the balanced strong-factor rank-one second-order remainder is \(o(\Delta_{\mathrm{CY},n}(K))\); if so, \(\Delta^{\dagger}\) must use the smaller attained scale.  The common-subclass and score-stability restrictions apply only to the converse witness and do not assume any remainder lower bound.
proposed_statement_changes.reason: The old question neither distinguished the note-specific event-transfer class from the published approximate-rank class nor conditioned coverage on the score-stability control that the proved generic theorem requires.  The proposed claim adds that necessary condition and requires the converse witness to lie in the common subclass with stable scores, so any eventual negative result transfers upward without assuming the nonlinear-remainder crux.

proposed_assumptions.reason: The event-transfer model is the zero-approximation specialization of the ambient mean decomposition.
proposed_assumptions.not_crux: This only records the absence of approximation bias and asserts no estimator-remainder property.

proposed_assumptions.reason: The exact factorization was previously embedded in the global symbol definition of \(M^0\).  Making it an event-transfer member property permits an honest comparison with the published approximate-rank class while preserving every event-score formula.
proposed_assumptions.not_crux: This only relocates the already maintained exact-factor restriction; it asserts no remainder, covariance, or coverage conclusion.

proposed_assumptions.reason: This is the published approximate-rank decomposition needed to state the external class rather than silently substituting the note's exact-rank class.
proposed_assumptions.not_crux: It defines the published comparison domain and does not supply the event-curve remainder lower bound.

proposed_assumptions.reason: The leading component in the published approximate-rank decomposition has rank \(r\).
proposed_assumptions.not_crux: This is a model-rank restriction and contains no inference conclusion.

proposed_assumptions.condition: Writing \(M^\star=U_n^\star D_n^\star(V_n^\star)^\top\) as a compact rank-\(r\) singular-value decomposition, \(\max\{(N/r)\|U_n^\star\|_{2,\infty}^2,(T/r)\|V_n^\star\|_{2,\infty}^2\}\le\bar\mu\) for every \(n\).
proposed_assumptions.reason: This records that the published class uses global singular-vector incoherence, in contrast with the note's blockwise index.
proposed_assumptions.not_crux: It is a source-class regularity condition and contains no simultaneous-band conclusion.

proposed_assumptions.condition: There is a fixed \(C_\kappa<\infty\) such that \(\sigma_1(M^\star)/\sigma_r(M^\star)\le C_\kappa\) for every \(n\).
proposed_assumptions.reason: This separately records the global condition-number bound in the published class.
proposed_assumptions.not_crux: It is a source-class conditioning restriction and contains no simultaneous-band conclusion.

proposed_assumptions.condition: For every \(n\), there is a centered sub-Gaussian law \(F_n\) with variance \(\sigma_n^2\in[\underline\sigma^2,\bar\sigma^2]\) such that \(\{e_{it}:i\le N,t\le T\}\) are i.i.d. with law \(F_n\).
proposed_assumptions.reason: The published class's homoskedastic noise condition must remain distinct from the note's row-heteroskedastic event-transfer condition.
proposed_assumptions.not_crux: This is a published sampling restriction, not the missing growing-dimensional remainder argument.

proposed_assumptions.reason: This is hypothesis (i) of the published scalar staggered-adoption theorem.
proposed_assumptions.not_crux: It is a published scalar-functional premise, not a simultaneous event-curve remainder condition.

proposed_assumptions.reason: This is hypothesis (ii) of the published scalar staggered-adoption theorem.
proposed_assumptions.not_crux: It is a published scalar-functional premise, not a growing-dimensional approximation theorem.

proposed_assumptions.reason: This is hypothesis (iii) of the published scalar staggered-adoption theorem.
proposed_assumptions.not_crux: It is a published scalar-functional block-size premise and asserts no attained remainder.

proposed_assumptions.condition:
For every such functional and every source subgroup \(l\), the approximation condition is
\[
 \max_{i\in\mathcal U_l,t\in\mathcal T_l}|m_{it}^R|
 =o\!\left(\frac{\sigma}{\kappa^{5/2}\mu r
 \max\{\sqrt{N_0},\sqrt{T_{d_l}}\}}\right),
\]
proposed_assumptions.reason: This is hypothesis (iv) of the published scalar staggered-adoption theorem.
proposed_assumptions.not_crux: It controls published approximation bias and does not assume the event-transfer nonlinear remainder.

proposed_assumptions.condition:
For every such functional, there are fixed \(0<c_1\le c_2<\infty\) for which the global Gram-balance condition is
\[

proposed.statement:
Fix \(n\).  For \(g\in E_k\), let \(b_{gk,q}\) denote the expression inside square brackets in the definition of \(c_{kq}\), let
\[
 \widehat\tau_{gk}=n_g^{-1}\sum_{i\in I_g}(Y_{i,g+k}-\widehat m^0_{i,g+k}),
 \qquad
 \tau_{gk}=n_g^{-1}\sum_{i\in I_g}\tau_{i,g+k},
\]
and define the exact block remainder \(r_{gk}\) by
\[
 \widehat\tau_{gk}-\tau_{gk}
 =\sum_{q\in\mathcal Q_n^{\mathrm{IF}}}b_{gk,q}e_q+r_{gk}.
\]
Then the eligible-unit aggregation obeys the exact eventwise identity
\[
 D_n^{-1}(\widehat\tau-\tau^{\mathrm{event}})
 =\left(\sum_{q\in\mathcal Q_n^{\mathrm{IF}}}a_{kq}e_q/\sigma_q\right)_{k\in\mathcal K_n}+\rho_n,
 \qquad
 \rho_{n,k}=s_k^{-1}\sum_{g\in E_k}\frac{n_g}{N_k}r_{gk}.
\]
For \(C>0\), define
\[
 \mathcal A_n(C)=\bigcap_{k\in\mathcal K_n}\bigcap_{g\in E_k}
 \{|r_{gk}|\le C R_{gk}^{\mathrm{CY}}\}.
\]
On \(\mathcal A_n(C)\), the deterministic implication
\[
 \|\rho_n\|_\infty\le C\Delta_{\mathrm{CY},n}(K)
\]
holds.  In the i.i.d. homoskedastic source submodel in which every eligible block satisfies the hypotheses of Choi--Yuan Proposition A.4, there are constants \(C,C_0<\infty\), common to the eligible blocks for all sufficiently large \(n\), such that
\[
 P_n\{\mathcal A_n(C)^c\}
 \le C_0\sum_{k\in\mathcal K_n}\sum_{g\in E_k}
 \min\{N_{gk}^{-9},T_g^{-9}\}.
\]
No assertion that the last sum vanishes, and no uniform \(O_{P_n}(\Delta_{\mathrm{CY},n}(K))\) assertion over \(\mathfrak M^{\mathrm{CY}}\), is made.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The dependency now records that the exact Choi--Yuan aggregation is the source-specific remainder-event specialization of the generic transfer theorem; it still claims only the unsimplified finite union bound.

proposed.statement:
Using the second-order staircase alignment handle, derive a primitive block-ratio expression \(\Delta_n^{\dagger}(K;\eta_n)\) and constants \(0<c<C<\infty\), common across \(n\), such that
\[
 c\Delta_n^{\dagger}(K;\eta_n)\le\Delta_n^*(K;\eta_n)
 \le C\Delta_n^{\dagger}(K;\eta_n)
\]
for every vanishing tail sequence \(\eta_n\), where \(\Delta_n^*\) is optimized over the explicitly defined slice \(\mathcal M_n^{\mathrm{CY},0}\) of the baseline event-transfer class \(\mathfrak M^{\mathrm{CY},0}\).  Establish the conditional coverage frontier in this finite-slice experiment: if there is a deterministic \(h_n\downarrow0\) such that
\[
 \sup_{P_n\in\mathcal M_n^{\mathrm{CY},0}}
 P_n\{\mathcal B_n(h_n)^c\}\to0,
 \qquad h_n\log^2(4K)\to0,
\]
then \(\Delta_n^{\dagger}(K;\eta_n)\sqrt{\log(2K)}\to0\) must imply \(\sup_{P_n\in\mathcal M_n^{\mathrm{CY},0}}\Gamma_n(P_n)\to0\).  Conversely, for every primitive candidate \(\beta\) with \(\beta\triangleleft\Delta^{\dagger}\) and \(\beta_n(K)\sqrt{\log(2K)}\to0\) along a subsequence on which \(\Delta_n^{\dagger}(K;\eta_n)\sqrt{\log(2K)}\) is bounded away from zero, construct one complete staggered low-rank triangular array
\[
 (P_n)_{n\ge1}\in\mathfrak M^{\mathrm{CY,com}}
 \subseteq\mathfrak M^{\mathrm{CY},0}\cap\mathfrak M^{\mathrm{CY,pub}}
\]
such that \(P_n\in\mathcal M_n^{\mathrm{CY},0}\), \(\delta_n(P_n;\eta_n)\ge c\Delta_n^{\dagger}(K;\eta_n)\), \(\liminf_n\Gamma_n(P_n)>0\), and, for some deterministic \(h_n\downarrow0\),
\[
 P_n\{\mathcal B_n(h_n)^c\}\to0,
 \qquad h_n\log^2(4K)\to0.
\]
The derivation must first test whether the balanced strong-factor rank-one second-order remainder is \(o(\Delta_{\mathrm{CY},n}(K))\); if so, \(\Delta^{\dagger}\) must use the smaller attained scale.  The common-subclass and score-stability restrictions apply only to the converse witness and do not assume any remainder lower bound.

open_obligations.what_is_open: The exact second-order Choi--Yuan remainder on a balanced rank-one complete array in the common subclass, a matching lower bound for its \(1-\eta_n\) quantile with signs aligned across horizons, and preservation of the displayed feasible score-stability rate on that witness.
open_obligations.obstruction: The published \(R_{gk}^{\mathrm{CY}}\) is an upper perturbation envelope, not an attained expansion.  The frozen estimator definition omits the nuclear-norm objective's tuning sequence, KKT solution map, exact debiasing formula, and growing rowwise loading control needed to compute the mandated second-order term and certify the witness's score stability.  The common-subclass repair strengthens legality but supplies none of those missing estimator identities.
open_obligations.attempted: The balanced rank-one coefficient calculation determines only the first-order score and its shared-cell covariance.  The generic transfer proves sufficiency for any attained modulus \(u_n\), and the Choi--Yuan block result gives a one-sided event implication, but successive norm inequalities provide neither a reverse bound nor a sign-controlled undercoverage array.  The published-only approximate-rank witness cannot be used because the directive correctly requires the converse inside the common exact-rank subclass.
open_obligations.partial_result:
The definitions identify the exact but nonprimitive event-transfer frontier:
\[
 \Delta_n^*(K;\eta_n)
 =\sup_{P_n\in\mathcal M_n^{\mathrm{CY},0}}
 \inf\{d\ge0:P_n(\|\rho_n\|_\infty>d)\le\eta_n\}.
\]
The generic transfer theorem proves that any deterministic \(u_n\) satisfying
\[
 \sup_{P_n\in\mathcal M_n^{\mathrm{CY},0}}
 P_n\{\|\rho_n\|_\infty>u_n\}\le\eta_n
\]
is a sufficient simultaneous remainder modulus, subject separately to the displayed score-stability probabilities.  The Choi--Yuan specialization gives the computable implication
\[
 \mathcal A_n(C)\subseteq
 \{\|\rho_n\|_\infty\le C\Delta_{\mathrm{CY},n}(K)\}.
\]
Thus, if the unsimplified simultaneous block-failure probability were uniformly at most \(\eta_n\), one would obtain the one-sided bound \(\Delta_n^*(K;\eta_n)\le C\Delta_{\mathrm{CY},n}(K)\).  No reverse inequality follows.  The class-comparison proposition additionally proves that a future lower witness constructed in \(\mathfrak M^{\mathrm{CY,com}}\) is automatically legal for both the baseline event-transfer experiment and the published approximate-rank class, so its converse transfers upward.

More precisely, if the requested upper equivalence \(\Delta_n^*(K;\eta_n)\le C\Delta_n^\dagger(K;\eta_n)\) were established, then the definition of the infimum implies
\[
 \sup_{P_n\in\mathcal M_n^{\mathrm{CY},0}}
 P_n\{\|\rho_n\|_\infty>(C+1)\Delta_n^\dagger(K;\eta_n)\}
 \le\eta_n. \tag{1}
\]
Indeed, for each law the infimum is at most \(C\Delta_n^\dagger\), so some admissible threshold lies strictly below \((C+1)\Delta_n^\dagger\), and the tail probability is nonincreasing in the threshold.  Under the score-stability conditions displayed in the narrowed question, apply the generic theorem with \(u_n=(C+1)\Delta_n^\dagger(K;\eta_n)\).  The corrected cell-leverage envelope bounds its Gaussian term by \(C(\varepsilon_n^{\mathrm{lev}})^{1/4}\), equation (1) bounds the remainder-event failure by \(\eta_n\), and all other displayed terms vanish.  Therefore
\[
 \Delta_n^\dagger(K;\eta_n)\sqrt{\log(2K)}\to0
 \quad\Longrightarrow\quad
 \sup_{P_n\in\mathcal M_n^{\mathrm{CY},0}}\Gamma_n(P_n)\to0
\]
under that score-stability condition.  Thus the narrowed upper transfer is reduced completely to the requested primitive upper equivalence; the unresolved content is its primitive evaluation and the score-stable common-subclass lower witness.

prose_updates.tldr: The note now separates a note-specific event-transfer class from the incomparable published Choi--Yuan approximate-rank scalar-functional class.  The main finite-error result is a generic remainder-event transfer: the sign-expanded event score satisfies the Chernozhukov--Chetverikov--Kato--Koike 2022 fourth-root Gaussian bound under log power five, while nonlinear remainder and feasible-score errors remain explicit event probabilities.  Choi--Yuan Proposition A.4 supplies only the specialization \(u=C\Delta_{\mathrm{CY},n}(K)\) on \(\mathcal A_n(C)\), with its unsimplified blockwise union bound.  Growing-curve coverage remains conditional, and the attainable common-subclass converse remains open.

project_justification.gap: Published Choi--Yuan inference permits approximate rank but is organized around global geometry, i.i.d. homoskedastic noise, and one scalar group-at-time functional under six hypotheses.  It does not provide a simultaneous growing-block probability or the rowwise feasible-score rate for this event curve.  Generic high-dimensional Gaussian approximation controls the linear score but cannot create those panel-specific controls.
project_justification.niche: The useful object is a generic remainder-event transfer for the exact primitive-cell event score, followed by an honest Choi--Yuan specialization.  This separates universal Gaussian approximation from estimator-specific block remainders and makes class scope auditable.
project_justification.fill: The note proves exact eligible-unit aggregation and full staircase covariance, verifies the 2022 Gaussian theorem with \(B_n=C\sqrt mL_n(K)\), unit coordinate variances, fourth moments bounded by \(CmL_n(K)^2\), and a \(\psi_1\) envelope, and obtains error \(C\{L_n(K)^2\log^5((p\vee3)m)\}^{1/4}\).  The finite coverage map adds \(P_n\{\mathcal R_n(u)^c\}\), score-event failure, anti-concentration, and covariance-stability terms.  Proposition A.4 is then used only through \(\mathcal A_n(C)\subseteq\mathcal R_n(C\Delta_{\mathrm{CY},n}(K))\).

sampling_model.units: The primary domain is a complete triangular array in the note-specific event-transfer class: deterministic exact-rank factor means, blockwise uniform geometry, independent centered row-heteroskedastic sub-Gaussian errors, variance replication, and log-power-five cell leverage.  The separately defined published Choi--Yuan class permits \(M^0=M^\star+M^R\), uses global geometry and i.i.d. homoskedastic noise, and is incomparable with the event-transfer class.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: The feasible protocol still uses blockwise Choi--Yuan completion and debiasing, leave-one-cell-out untreated residuals, unit variance estimates, plug-in influence coefficients, and Gaussian multipliers.  Oracle variance concentration is proved, whereas the nonlinear remainder is represented by \(\mathcal R_n(u)\) and the normalized score-loading discrepancy by \(\mathcal B_n(h)\); their stochastic rates are not supplied by the class definition.

prose_updates.related_work: Choi and Yuan, \cite{ChoiYuan2024MNAR}, allow \(M^0=M^\star+M^R\), impose global singular-vector geometry and i.i.d. homoskedastic sub-Gaussian noise, and state staggered Theorem 3.2 for a scalar group-at-time functional under six hypotheses.  Their supplementary Proposition A.4 gives a one-block entrywise expansion; aggregation over the growing eligible block family yields only the unsimplified finite union bound used here.  Chernozhukov, Chetverikov, Kato, and Koike, \cite{ChernozhukovChetverikovKatoKoike2022Improved}, Theorem 2.1, provide the singular-covariance-safe fourth-root Gaussian approximation with log power five used for the linear event score.  The 2023 log-cubed result is not used because its covariance nondegeneracy is unavailable for a staircase correlation matrix.  Chernozhukov, Chetverikov, and Kato, \cite{ChernozhukovChetverikovKato2013Maxima}, Lemma 3.1, supply the singular-safe Gaussian comparison, and \cite{ChernozhukovChetverikovKato2014Bands} supplies anti-concentration.  Choi, Kwon, and Liao, \cite{ChoiKwonLiao2024Completion}, analyze fixed functionals rather than the frozen growing rowwise score error.  Ben-Michael and Feller, \cite{BenMichaelFeller2026Discussion}, motivate the right-to-carry event curve; Callaway and Sant'Anna, \cite{CallawaySantAnna2021DID}, obtain simultaneous staggered paths under parallel trends rather than this low-rank MNAR transfer.
prose_updates.interpretation: For a right-to-carry event curve, researchers may choose a deterministic diagnostic threshold \(u_n\), verify a simultaneous remainder event \(\mathcal R_n(u_n)\), and combine it with the score-stability diagnostic.  The common critical value is honest when the explicit finite-error terms vanish.  Using the published Choi--Yuan ratios sets \(u_n=C\Delta_{\mathrm{CY},n}(K)\) only on the joint block event; the paper does not claim that event is uniformly likely.
prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: The updated linear approximation now needs \(L_n(K)^2\log^5((p\vee3)m)\to0\), with balanced-loading elbow \(\log(Km)=o(m^{1/5})\).  The unresolved limitations are estimator-specific: no frozen premise makes the growing Choi--Yuan block union probability vanish or controls the feasible rowwise score discrepancy.  The published approximate-rank class also introduces an \(M^R\) bias absent from the event-transfer expansion, so upper-band validity does not transfer to that full class.  Finally, the KKT-level second-order map needed to test attainment of \(\Delta_{\mathrm{CY},n}(K)\) is not present in the frozen primitives.
prose_updates.honest_scope: The delivered theorem is a generic finite-error transfer on the baseline event-transfer class, not unconditional feasible growing-curve coverage.  It permits singular staircase correlation and uses the log-power-five 2022 Gaussian approximation.  Asymptotic \(1-\alpha\) coverage is asserted only along arrays for which \(P_n\{\mathcal R_n(u_n)^c\}\to0\), \(P_n\{\mathcal B_n(h_n)^c\}\to0\), \(u_n\sqrt{\log(2p)}\to0\), and \(h_n\log^2(2p)\to0\).  Choi--Yuan supplies a blockwise specialization, not those probability limits.  The event-transfer and published classes are incomparable; a future converse must be built in their common exact-rank rank-one subclass, and approximate-rank upper validity needs a separate bias remainder.

statement_notes.gap: Neither class contains the other because approximate rank and i.i.d. homoskedastic noise cut in opposite directions from exact rank and row heteroskedasticity.
statement_notes.consumer: Any eventual lower witness in the common subclass transfers to the published class, while upper-band claims remain confined to the event-transfer domain unless approximation bias is added.
